content: Arb, which is short for arbitrage, refers to a system of hand signals specifically designed to convey buy and sell information in an open outcry trading environment. This system is widely utilized in various financial exchanges, including the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. Traders employ these hand signals rapidly across the trading floor to execute sales or purchases. When a trader gestures with their palms facing outward and their hands extended away from their body, it signifies an intention to sell. Conversely, when a trader positions their palms inward and raises their hands, it indicates a desire to buy. Numbers are communicated through specific hand gestures. For instance, numbers one through five are signaled using one hand, while numbers six through ten are gestured in a similar manner but with the hand held sideways at a 90-degree angle. For example, extending the index finger sideways represents six, two fingers represent seven, and so on. Additionally, numbers gestured from the forehead represent blocks of ten. It is important to note that the exact rules governing these gestures may differ between exchanges or even between trading floors within the same exchange. However, the fundamental purpose of these gestures—to facilitate efficient communication of trading intentions—remains consistent.
